# The AI Semiconductor Boom and What Could End It with Stacy Rasgon | The Real Eisman Playbook Ep 63

First listed: 2026-06-08 | Evaluation cutoff: 2026-11-10

[Back to library](../README.md)

## Source versions

- [YouTube: The AI Semiconductor Boom and What Could End It with Stacy Rasgon | The Real Eisman Playbook Ep 63](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=imrBSvXepYI) - 2026-06-08
- [Substack: The AI Semiconductor Boom and What Could End It with Stacy Rasgon | The Real Eisman Playbook Ep 63](https://realeismanplaybook.substack.com/p/the-ai-semiconductor-boom-and-what) - 2026-06-08

Earliest listed publication among matched versions, not proof of an unedited contemporaneous archive. Claim timestamps refer to the reviewed version.

## Summary

Stacy Rasgon describes AI demand spreading from GPUs into CPU, memory, networking and equipment bottlenecks. He upgrades AMD, remains constructive on Broadcom and NVIDIA, and distinguishes Intel's improved narrative from proven manufacturing economics. Eisman owns NVIDIA and endorses the continuing infrastructure cycle. They reject simplistic immediate GPU obsolescence while identifying weak eventual returns and power limits as risks. Later supplier earnings support demand acceleration, but long-horizon revenue, EPS and investment-return claims remain open.

Claims are assessed individually. Empirical premises are not treated as successful forecasts. Unverified magnitudes and causal stories remain unresolved; subjective investment judgments are not assigned directional wins.

Further verification: Recheck the original data and subsequent realized outcomes.

- [AMD third quarter 2026 results](https://ir.amd.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/1303/amd-reports-third-quarter-2026-financial-results) (2026-11-03): Revenue $13.377b grew 45%, Data Center $8.5b grew 97%, non-GAAP EPS $2.09. Actual CPU/GPU growth supports demand, while $17b Q4 revenue remains guidance and does not resolve 2027-2028 earnings forecasts.
- [Broadcom third quarter fiscal 2026 results](https://investors.broadcom.com/news-releases/news-release-details/broadcom-inc-announces-third-quarter-fiscal-year-2026-financial) (2026-09-02): AI semiconductor revenue $16.7b grew 221%; infrastructure software revenue $8.752b grew 29%. Total revenue $29.591b and FCF $13.665b. These results support continued demand, not the full 2027 AI revenue target.
- [NVIDIA second quarter fiscal 2027 results](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-announces-financial-results-for-second-quarter-fiscal-2027/) (2026-08-26): Revenue $96.221b grew 106%, Data Center $89b grew 117%, gross margin 75%. Actual growth continued accelerating beyond the May report. These supplier revenues do not prove customers' ultimate capital returns.

### 015. Lengthening depreciation lives raises current earnings mechanically, but does not by itself prove that asset-life estimates are illegitimate.

**Right** | Steve Eisman | analytical principle | major

[Source at 24:08-24:44](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=imrBSvXepYI&t=1448s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

The conditional relationship follows from the explicit assumptions; it does not establish that those assumptions hold in observed markets.

Conditional reasoning: Annual expense is depreciable cost divided by useful life. A longer life reduces current expense and increases current pretax profit, while lifetime total depreciation is unchanged. Economic validity requires evidence about useful service life.

Assessment test: Inspect the relevant original financial, operational or economic data and compare the claimed mechanism with competing explanations.

Further verification: Recheck the original data and subsequent realized outcomes.

## Framework and tools

- Distinguish earnings revisions from multiple expansion.
- Inspect bottlenecks across the entire supply chain.
- Treat reported margin changes separately from impairment base effects.
- Use GPU rental prices and utilization to assess useful life.
- Separate temporary digestion from permanent ROI failure.
- Treat management language, warrants and capex announcements as evidence requiring interpretation.

Tools and charts discussed, not a complete visual inspection:

- SOX forward earnings and P/E decomposition
- NVIDIA customer reporting change
- CPU/GPU rack ratios and agent workload illustration
- GPU rental rates by generation
- AMD EPS scenarios and warrant milestones
- Intel yields and packaging opportunity
- Capex and power availability

## Source cautions

Stacy Rasgon supplies technical explanations, analyst ratings and numerical forecasts. Eisman asks questions, discloses NVIDIA ownership and gives the closing endorsement; guest upgrades are not attributed to Eisman.
- Rasgon corrects Eisman's gross-margin comparison in real time; the correction is preserved.
- Rasgon explicitly says fixed CPU/GPU attachment ratios are an imperfect heuristic.
- The $600 AMD warrant threshold is a vesting condition, not an unconditional price target.
- May 25, 2023 refers to market reaction; the earnings release was the prior evening.
- Qualcomm and Intel rumors remain unconfirmed in the extracted claims.
